MLforSEO Academy · Semantic AI-powered SEO Keyword Research

Content Briefs Generator

Turn your Semantic Keyword Universe sheet into up to 20 content briefs at a time, combining the sheet's keyword, entity and SERP data with suggestions from OpenAI.

What you need
Your Semantic Keyword Universe Google Sheet shared as 'Anyone with the link can view', a Google Cloud API key with the Google Sheets API enabled, and your OpenAI API key
Cost
Free to use; OpenAI bills your key per request. Each brief makes 7 requests: roughly 6 US cents a brief with GPT-5.6 Terra, under 1 cent with GPT-6 Luna. Reading the sheet costs nothing.
Feed it
The URL of your keyword universe sheet, up to three of its topics, and how many briefs you want (1 to 20)
You get back
A ZIP of briefs as Markdown-formatted .txt files, one per keyword, which you can also preview and download one at a time

How to use it

  1. Share your keyword universe sheet so anyone with the link can view it. The tool reads the template's tabs by name, so keep them as they are.
  2. Paste the sheet URL and your Google API key, then press Load topics.
  3. Pick up to three topics and set how many briefs you want.
  4. Add your OpenAI key, choose a model and press Generate.
  5. Download the ZIP, and check every AI section before a writer works from it.

Worth knowing. The AI sections are suggestions, not research: competitor gaps and internal-link targets are written from the keyword alone, so check them against the live results and your own site.

MLforSEO · Semantic AI-powered SEO Keyword Research

Content Briefs Generator

Turn your Semantic Keyword Universe sheet into content briefs: it picks the highest-potential keywords for up to three topics, gathers what the sheet knows about each one, adds suggestions from OpenAI and packs the briefs into a ZIP.

1 · Your keyword universe

The Google Sheet you built with the course’s Semantic Keyword Universe template. Share it as Anyone with the link can view: an API key can only read sheets shared that way.
Topics load from the Topics and Descriptions tab once both fields are filled in.
Which tabs it reads
  • Keyword Categorisationrequired
    metrics, intent, format, depth, persona, entities, n-grams
  • Topics and Descriptionsrequired
    the topic list and each topic’s description
  • Keywords to Topics with sBERT
    which keywords belong to which topic
  • Keyword Suggestions
    related terms, by seed keyword
  • Entity Sentiment Data
    attributes of the core entity and sub-entity
  • Semantic Entity Relationships
    semantically related entities
  • SERP Features Analysis
    intent mapping, SERP features, content formats
  • Google/YouTube Autosuggest Terms
    autosuggest terms, by seed keyword
  • Query Paths - PAA
    People Also Ask questions and snippets
  • Query Paths - Suggested Topics
    session and context signals
  • Bulk Google SERP
    the top five ranking pages

2 · Your OpenAI key

Used for the AI sections of each brief: query fan-out, user journeys, personas, formats, competitor gaps, internal linking, titles and headings.

3 · What to brief

Pick up to three topics. Briefs are shared out evenly across them, highest-potential keywords first: search volume weighed against competition.
